# Data Models & Persistence — Web

*Generated by the BMad document-project workflow — deep scan, 2026-07-17.*

## Overview

There is no database in Telar. Every persisted entity is a JSON, NDJSON, or YAML file under a single root directory, `TELAR_HOME` (default `~/.telar`).

**The schemas and the read/write functions live in `packages/core` (`@telar/core`), not in `apps/web`.** `apps/web` depends on `@telar/core` via `workspace:*` (`apps/web/package.json`) and, in the common case, runs it **in-process**: Next.js API route handlers under `apps/web/app/api/**` import functions directly from `@telar/core` (e.g. `looms.ts`, `manifest.ts`, `dispatcher.ts`, `accounts.ts`) and call them synchronously inside the request handler — there is no HTTP hop, no ORM, no client/server split for this data. Concretely: 60+ files under `apps/web/app` and `apps/web/components` import `@telar/core` (verified via `grep -rl "@telar/core" apps/web`), and `apps/web/app/api/looms/route.ts`, `apps/web/app/api/looms/[id]/accept/route.ts`, etc. call `listLooms()`, `acceptLoom()`, and friends straight from `../../../../packages/core/src/looms.ts`.

This file (`data-models-web.md`) is named for the web part's place in the generated doc set, but its subject — the persisted entities, their schemas, and their lifecycle — is the **shared** persistence layer owned by core. Where the web app additionally owns its own on-disk state (chat transcripts, permission rules, live-turn logs, pending OAuth flows — none of it zod-schema'd, all of it living alongside core's files under the same `TELAR_HOME`), that is called out explicitly in [Entities & Schemas](#entities--schemas) and is the one place this doc's scope is genuinely web-specific.

An out-of-process **runner** mode also exists (M5 scaffold: `packages/core/src/runner/*`) where a separate `telar-runner` process, not the Next.js server, owns loom execution and the web app talks to it over a bearer-token HTTP transport (`runner/http-transport.ts`) discovered via `~/.telar/runner.json`. Persistence itself is unaffected — both the in-process and out-of-process runner write through the exact same `@telar/core` store functions onto the exact same `TELAR_HOME` files.

See also: [./architecture-core.md](./architecture-core.md) for the engine/executor/weaver control flow that produces the state transitions this doc describes.

## Storage Architecture

### `TELAR_HOME` resolution

Every core store resolves the root the same way — `process.env.TELAR_HOME ?? path.join(os.homedir(), ".telar")` (`packages/core/src/manifest.ts:telarDir()`, re-implemented identically in `looms.ts`, `secrets.ts` imports it from `manifest.ts`, `accounts.ts`, `watches.ts`, `mcp-oauth.ts`). `apps/web/lib/permissions.ts` and `apps/web/lib/session-log.ts` mirror this same `process.env.TELAR_HOME ?? path.join(os.homedir(), ".telar")` expression locally.

`apps/web/lib/store.ts` follows the same root contract for chat history and the usage ledger, so an isolated `TELAR_HOME` keeps all of those writes together.

### Directory layout

| Path (under `TELAR_HOME`) | Owner | Format | Written by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `projects.json` | core | JSON | `manifest.ts` (`registerProject`/`unregisterProject`) |
| `accounts.json` | core | JSON | `accounts.ts` |
| `credentials.json` (mode 0600) | core | JSON | `secrets.ts` |
| `mcp-oauth.json` (mode 0600) | core | JSON | `mcp-oauth.ts` |
| `mcp-oauth-pending.json` (mode 0600) | **web** | JSON | `apps/web/lib/mcp-oauth-pending.ts` |
| `watches.json` | core | JSON | `watches.ts` |
| `permissions.json` | **web** | JSON | `apps/web/lib/permissions.ts` |
| `runner.json` / `runner.lock` (mode 0600 for `.json`) | core (M5) | JSON | `runner/runner-json.ts` |
| `looms/<id>/loom.json` | core | JSON | `looms.ts` (`saveLoom`, atomic tmp+rename) |
| `looms/<id>/events.ndjson` | core | NDJSON, append-only | `looms.ts` (`appendEvent`) |
| `looms/<id>/spec/*` (`contract.json`, `objective.md`, `steering.md`, `provenance.json`, free-form context files) | core | JSON/Markdown | `bundle.ts` |
| `looms/<id>/evidence/*` | core | binary/text | Verifier/Critic Panel agent runs |
| `looms/<id>/.runner-lease` | core (M5) | JSON | `runner/lease.ts` |
| `looms/<id>/.started` | core | sentinel (O_EXCL) | `dispatcher.ts` |
| `worktrees/telar-wt-<id>-<n>/` | core | git worktree | `vcs.ts` |
| `ultra/<runId>/manifest.json`, `events.ndjson`, `agents/<ordinal>.ndjson`, `journal.jsonl`, `script.js` | core (Ultra sub-engine) | JSON/NDJSON/JS | `ultra/storage.ts`, `ultra/journal.ts` |
| `chats.json` | **web** | JSON | `apps/web/lib/store.ts` |
| `usage.ndjson` | **web** | NDJSON, append-only | `apps/web/lib/store.ts` (`logUsage`) |
| `sessions/<sessionId>/live.ndjson` | **web** | NDJSON, truncated per turn | `apps/web/lib/session-log.ts` |
| `runs/` (legacy) | core | — | migrated once to `looms/` by `looms.ts:ensureMigrated` |

Per-project files, tracked or gitignored inside the project's own repo (not under `TELAR_HOME`):

| Path (repo-relative) | Tracked? | Schema | Written by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `telar.yaml` | tracked | `ProjectManifest` (`schemas.ts`) | `manifest.ts` (`writeManifest`, `createProject`) |
| `servers.yaml` | tracked | `ServersConfig` (`schemas.ts`) | authored by hand or by the setup agent |
| `.telar/servers.yaml` | gitignored | `ServersConfig` | `servers.ts:writeAcceptedServersConfig`, called only from `answerBlocked` after a human answer |
| `runbook.md` | tracked | free text, no schema | authored by hand |
| `.telar/runbook.md` | gitignored | free text | `servers.ts:writeAcceptedRunbook`, human-accepted |

### The `telar.yaml` project manifest

Loaded/validated by `manifest.ts:loadManifest` (YAML.parse → `ProjectManifest.safeParse`, throws on malformed YAML or a schema-invalid file) and written by `writeManifest` (YAML.stringify, atomic tmp+rename via `atomicWrite`). Full field table — see [`ProjectManifest`](#projectmanifest) below.

`getProject()` (`manifest.ts`) **self-heals**: if `telar.yaml` is missing on disk (e.g. wiped by a build agent's `git clean`/`checkout`/`reset`) but the registry (`projects.json`) still holds a cached copy from the last successful read, it rewrites `telar.yaml` from that cache rather than failing. A present-but-invalid manifest still throws — only *absence* is healed. Every call to `getProject` also refreshes the registry cache if the live manifest has drifted (`isDeepStrictEqual` check against the cached copy).

## Entities & Schemas

All zod schemas below are defined in `packages/core/src/schemas.ts` unless otherwise noted. Field lists are abbreviated to what a feature author needs; read the cited symbol for the full shape (comments in `schemas.ts` are extensive and load-bearing — read them before changing a field).

### Core-owned (zod-validated)

#### `ProjectManifest` — `telar.yaml`

Schema: `ProjectManifest` (`packages/core/src/schemas.ts:227`). Store: `manifest.ts`.

| Field | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | — | registry key |
| `root` | `string` | — | absolute path to the repo |
| `adapter` | `"plain" \| "bmad"` | `"plain"` | |
| `account` | `string` | `"personal"` | `AccountProfile.name` — routes billing |
| `charterPolicy` | `"auto" \| "human-required-for-epics" \| "human-required"` | `"human-required-for-epics"` | when a drafted Charter pauses for human review |
| `baseBranch` | `string` | `"main"` | pin threads fork from |
| `gates` | `{ name, run }[]` | `[]` | named shell gates, run by `gates.ts:runGate` |
| `guardrails.disallowedTools` | `string[]` | `[]` | folded into every project-scoped agent's disallow list |
| `guardrails.protectedPaths` | `string[]` | `[]` | surfaced to the builder + checked post-build against git-derived touched files |
| `urls.dev` / `urls.preview` / `urls.prod` | `string?` | — | |
| `designRules` | `string?` | — | path to a design-guidelines doc for the Verifier |
| `devCommand` | `string?` | — | starts the dev server on a free port when no `urls.dev` |
| `verifyCommand` | `string?` | — | M11 human-answered strategy: an exit-code-proving command, used when no server-lane exists |
| `templateDb` | `string?` | — | template DB the frozen-lane verify clones from |
| `mcpServers` | `Record<string, McpServerConfig>` | `{}` | secret-free; see `McpServerConfig` |

#### `RegistryEntry` — `projects.json`

Type (not zod, plain TS): `RegistryEntry` (`manifest.ts:14`) = `{ name, root, addedAt, manifest? }`. Keyed by project name. `manifest` is the self-heal cache described above.

#### `AccountProfile` / `AccountRegistry` — `accounts.json`

Schema: `AccountProfile` (`schemas.ts:23`) = `{ name, provider?, authMode?, configDir?, tokenEnv?, displayTier? }`. Store shape `AccountRegistry` (`accounts.ts:18`, plain TS) = `{ version, default, accounts: AccountProfile[] }`. Seeded non-destructively on first read (`accounts.ts:seed()`) from whatever provider logins already exist on the machine. `configDir` is stored home-relative (`"~/.claude-work"`) for portability across machines and expanded at use time.

#### `SecretFile` — `credentials.json` (mode 0600)

Plain TS type in `secrets.ts:10`: `{ version, tokens: Record<string, string> }`. One token per key. Keys are either an account name, or a namespaced MCP secret `mcp:<project>:<key>`, or the mirrored MCP-OAuth access token `mcp:<project>:<server>` (mirrored by `mcp-oauth.ts:mirrorAccessToken`).

#### `McpOAuthRecord` / OAuth store — `mcp-oauth.json` (mode 0600)

Plain TS type `McpOAuthRecord` (`mcp-oauth.ts:43`) = `{ project, server, resource, as: AuthServerMeta, client: OAuthClient, tokens: OAuthTokens }`. Store shape (`mcp-oauth.ts:558`, unexported) `{ version, records: Record<"mcp-oauth:<project>:<server>", McpOAuthRecord> }`. Read/write via `getRecord`/`putRecord`/`deleteRecord`.

#### `Watch` / `WatchFile` — `watches.json`

Plain TS type `Watch` (`watches.ts:11`) = `{ id, loomId, sessionId, triggerStates: WorkUnitState[], createdAt, status: "active"|"fired"|"cancelled", lastFiredState? }`. `DEFAULT_TRIGGER_STATES = ["needs-review","blocked","failed","done","ready"]`. One active watch per `(sessionId, loomId)` pair — a new `addWatch` for the same pair replaces the prior active one.

#### `Loom` / `AttemptRecord` / `RelaxedCoverage` — `looms/<id>/loom.json`

Plain TS type `Loom` (`looms.ts:72`) — the central runtime entity. Full field table:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `string` | `loom_<base36-ts>_<random>` |
| `project`, `kind`, `title`, `prompt`, `account` | `string` | `kind: "quickfix"\|"story"\|"custom"\|"verify"` |
| `state` | `WorkUnitState` | see [state table](#workunitstate) |
| `createdAt`, `updatedAt` | `number` | epoch ms |
| `attempts` | `AttemptRecord[]` | build/verify attempt history |
| `error` | `string \| null` | |
| `parentLoomId?` | `string` | set on a child thread — points at the woven root |
| `subGoalId?` | `string` | which `Charter.decomposition` node this child proves |
| `charter?` | `Charter` | present on a woven root |
| `draft?` | `boolean` | exists on disk but not listed/dispatched until `startLoomFromBundle` commits it |
| `contractRequired?` | `boolean` | sticky once a Verification Contract was required to start |
| `commit?` | `string` | the git sha `acceptLoom` landed |
| `acceptedOverride?` / `acceptedOverrideMissing?` | `boolean` / `string` | audited-override accept trail (L3) |
| `latestVerdict?` | `string` | informational result of the end-of-orchestration integration verify |
| `worktree?`, `baseSha?`, `consolidationBranch?` | `string` | M3 worktree isolation |
| `recoveryBranch?`, `worktreeRetained?` | `string` / `boolean` | M8 worktree recovery |
| `blockedReason?`, `blockedQuestion?` | `string` | M10.4 pre-flight park draft |
| `repairHistory?` | `RepairRound[]` | M4 auto-repair round log (root-only) |
| `workflow?` | `ThreadWorkflow` | M9 step DAG |
| `relaxedCoverage?` | `RelaxedCoverage[]` | B1 coverage-relaxation record, re-proven fail-closed at the top gate |
| `requirementsOffer?` | `{ items: EnvRequirement[] }` | D3 human-only requirements offer |

`AttemptRecord` (`looms.ts:42`): `{ n, role, model, startedAt, endedAt?, sessionId?, cwd?, verdict?: Verdict, verifierReport?: VerifierReport, panelReport?: PanelReport, gates?: GateResult[], humanJudged?: ContractAssertion[], costUsd? }`.

`RelaxedCoverage` (`looms.ts:200`): `{ kind: string, assertionIds: string[], note? }` — checked at the top gate by the pure function `uncoveredRelaxedIds()`.

Writes are atomic (`saveLoom`: tmp file + `renameSync`). Path traversal in `id` is rejected by `loomDir()` before any fs call.

#### `LoomEvent` — `looms/<id>/events.ndjson`

Plain TS type `LoomEvent` (`looms.ts:40`) = `{ ts: number, type: string, ...rest }`. Append-only, one JSON object per line, tailed incrementally by line offset (`readEvents(id, afterLine)`). No queue/broker — the web app polls this file directly (e.g. `apps/web/app/api/looms/[id]/events/route.ts`).

#### `VerificationContract` / `ContractAssertion` — `looms/<id>/spec/contract.json`

Schemas: `VerificationContract` (`schemas.ts:532`) = `{ version, assertions: ContractAssertion[], synthesized? }`; `ContractAssertion` (`schemas.ts:510`) = `{ id, subGoalId?, description, type: AssertionType, expected?, expectedFile?, observable?, blocker, subjective? }`. `AssertionType` ∈ `golden-diff | value-equality | schema-match | contains | live-critic | command | gate | db`. Validated by `validateContract()` (falsifiability rules — every non-live-critic assertion needs a concrete `expected`/`expectedFile`; `command`/`gate` reject a stray `observable`; a `command.expected` must satisfy `isRunnableShape()`). Written via `bundle.ts:writeContract`, which additionally enforces a co-sign gate (`contractLoosenings()`) once the loom has left `draft`.

#### `Provenance` — `looms/<id>/spec/provenance.json`

Schema: `Provenance` (`schemas.ts:722`) = `{ sessionId?, approvedBy, humanApprovedAt }`. Guarded by `assertProvenance()` (throws on blank `approvedBy` or non-positive `humanApprovedAt`). Settable only by a UI action, never the session agent.

#### `ServersConfig` / `ServiceConfig` — `servers.yaml` / `.telar/servers.yaml`

Schema: `ServersConfig` (`schemas.ts:870`) = `{ version, driver: "none"|"host-process", services: Record<name, ServiceConfig> }`. `ServiceConfig` (`schemas.ts:838`): `command`, `portStrategy: "fixed"|"dynamic"`, `port?`, `portInject?` (`PortInject` — `env`/`arg`/`file` discriminated union), `readyCheck?` (`ReadyCheck` — one-shot), `healthcheck?` (`HealthCheck` — ongoing, feeds the supervisor), `restartPolicy?`, `reset?`, `dependsOn`, `env`. Resolved two-tier by `servers.ts:resolveServersConfig` — `.telar/servers.yaml` (human-accepted, gitignored) wins over `servers.yaml` (repo-tracked) wins over `driver:"none"` default; first-existing-file wins, malformed at any tier throws.

#### `RunnerJson` / `RunnerLease` — `runner.json` / `looms/<id>/.runner-lease` (M5)

Plain TS types: `RunnerJson` (`runner/runner-json.ts:9`) = `{ pid, port, token }`, mode 0600. `RunnerLease` (`runner/lease.ts:13`) = `{ pid, token, ts }`, heartbeated by the runner while it owns a loom; freshness checked by `isLeaseFresh(lease, ttlMs, now)`.

#### `Charter` / `SubGoal` / `Budget` / `ScopeBoundary` / `RequirementsRecord` (embedded in `Loom.charter`, not a separate file)

Schema: `Charter` (`schemas.ts:439`) = `{ objective, proofStrategy, scope: ScopeBoundary, budget: Budget, decomposition: SubGoal[], version, approvedBy?, scopingSessionId?, rationale?, singleThread?, proofHints?, requirements?: RequirementsRecord }`. `SubGoal` (`schemas.ts:386`): `{ id, title, detail, proofStrategy, acceptanceCriteria, dependsOn, required, status, proofHints? }`. `RequirementsRecord` (`schemas.ts:433`) = `{ requirements: EnvRequirement[], detectedAt? }`; `EnvRequirement` (`schemas.ts:418`) = `{ name, kind, classification, detail?, satisfied, source? }`. These are not written to their own file — they live inside `loom.json`'s `charter` field and are persisted by the same `saveLoom()` write.

### Web-owned (plain TypeScript, not zod-validated)

These live under `TELAR_HOME` alongside core's stores but are read/written entirely from `apps/web/lib/*` — `@telar/core` has no schema or accessor for them.

#### `Chat` / `ChatMessage` / `Part` — `chats.json`

Type `Chat` (`apps/web/lib/store.ts:61`): `{ id, title, customTitle?, model, effort?, account, project?, permissionMode?, loomId?, role?: "planner"|"steerer"|"escalation", createdAt, updatedAt, costUsd, turns, archived?, inputTokens?, outputTokens?, cacheReadTokens?, cacheCreateTokens?, contextTokens?, messages: ChatMessage[] }`. `id` is the Claude Agent SDK session id (stable across resumes). `loomId`/`role` link a chat session to a loom in three roles: planning it, steering it, or discussing a blocked escalation — the session-side half of the loom lifecycle documented below. `Part` (`store.ts:13`) is a discriminated `text | tool` union carrying per-tool-call permission/agent-spawn/task-status metadata. Whole file rewritten per turn (`writeChats`, tmp+rename).

#### `UsageEntry` — `usage.ndjson`

Type `UsageEntry` (`store.ts:111`) = `{ ts, account, model, sessionId, inputTokens, outputTokens, cacheReadTokens, cacheCreateTokens, costUsd }`. Append-only via `logUsage()`; read back per-session via `usageLogBySession()` (mtime-cached).

#### Permission rules — `permissions.json`

Shape (`apps/web/lib/permissions.ts:55`): `Record<project, { allow: string[] }>`, entries are Claude-Code-style tool rule strings (`"Write"`, `"Bash(bun test:*)"`). Read/added/removed via `readRules`/`addRule`/`removeRule`.

#### `SessionLogEvent` — `sessions/<sessionId>/live.ndjson`

Type `SessionLogEvent` (`apps/web/lib/session-log.ts:20`) = `{ event: string, data: unknown }`. Truncated and re-opened at the start of every turn (`startSessionLog`); mirrors `looms.ts`'s event-log pattern but scoped to one chat session's in-flight turn, letting a reconnecting client tail the live SSE stream instead of waiting for the turn to finish.

#### `PendingFlow` — `mcp-oauth-pending.json` (mode 0600)

Type `PendingFlow` (`apps/web/lib/mcp-oauth-pending.ts:16`) = `{ project, server, ctx: ConnectContext, createdAt }`, `ConnectContext` imported from `@telar/core`'s `mcp-oauth.ts`. Keyed by OAuth `state`, TTL 10 minutes, swept on every access. Bridges the redirect round-trip of `beginConnect`/`completeConnect` (core) across a page reload or dev-server restart.

## Relationships & Lifecycle

### Entity graph

```
ProjectManifest (telar.yaml)  ──registered into──▶  projects.json (RegistryEntry)
        │
        │ name, account
        ▼
      Loom (loom.json)  ──parentLoomId──▶  Loom (root, woven)
        │  1:1                                  │ Charter.decomposition: SubGoal[]
        ▼                                        │ (one SubGoal per child, via subGoalId)
   spec/ (Spec Bundle)                           ▼
     contract.json  (VerificationContract)   child Loom × N  (one per required/optional SubGoal)
     objective.md, steering.md
     provenance.json (Provenance)
        │
        ▼
   attempts: AttemptRecord[]  (build/verify history, each with Verdict / VerifierReport / PanelReport / GateResult[])
        │
        ▼
   events.ndjson  (LoomEvent log — queued/scoping/decision/weave-rollup/accepted/...)

Chat (chats.json)  ──loomId, role──▶  Loom   (a session that planned/steered/discussed a loom)
Watch (watches.json)  ──loomId──▶  Loom, ──sessionId──▶ Chat  (fires a reactor notification on a trigger state)
```

### `WorkUnitState` and terminal states

Schema: `WorkUnitState` (`schemas.ts:184`).

| State | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `queued` | created, not yet dispatched |
| `scoping` | a read-only agent is drafting the `Charter` |
| `charter-review` | paused, awaiting human approval of a woven charter (`charterPolicy`-gated) |
| `preparing` | optional M5 setup-agent lane bring-up |
| `running` | building/fanning out threads |
| `verifying` | verify pass in flight (transient, folded into the attempt loop) |
| `ready` | verified, awaiting owner acceptance |
| `done` | terminal — accepted, landed |
| `needs-review` | terminal-adjacent — a root-only demotion from `ready` after a red top-gate re-verify; **never reached by a child thread** |
| `blocked` | paused on a missing prerequisite or human decision |
| `halted` | terminal |
| `failed` | terminal |
| `skipped` | terminal |

`TERMINAL_WORK_UNIT_STATES = {done, halted, failed, skipped}` (`schemas.ts:204`) — the single source of truth for "is it over?" across dispatcher cancel, boot-sweep, and the MCP session-slot logic.

### Who moves state (verified against code)

- `dispatcher.ts:startLoom` creates the loom `queued`, optionally routes through `scoping` (`scoping.ts:draftCharter`, read-only) and pauses at `charter-review` per `manifest.charterPolicy`.
- `dispatcher.ts:runWeaveWiring` / `weave.ts:runWeave` drive `preparing → running → ready/needs-review/blocked/failed/halted` for a woven root; a root never builds itself.
- `executor.ts:executeLoom`/`decide()` drive a **child** thread's own attempt loop (build → gates → verify → retry/done/needs-review/failed/escalate); a child never lands `needs-review` directly — every unresolved outcome escalates to `blocked`, and the weave lifts that to the root for orchestrator mediation.
- `weave.ts:rollupWeave` is the **sole path to `ready`** — every required `SubGoal`'s child must independently be `done` (or already `ready`); otherwise the root becomes `failed` (any required child failed) or `blocked` (enumerating every unmet required subgoal).
- The post-`ready` integration verify (`executor.ts:runIntegrationVerify` + `verify-thread.ts:runAutoRepair`) can demote `ready → needs-review` on a real red verdict; it runs strictly after the `ready` write and never touches any other state.
- **`looms.ts:acceptLoom` is the only writer of `state: "done"` anywhere in the codebase.** It:
  1. rejects a blank `by`;
  2. refuses a child loom outright (`parentLoomId` set — children are consumed by the weave rollup, never accepted directly);
  3. requires `state === "ready"` for a clean accept, or `{override: true, missing: "<non-blank>"}` for any other state (stamping `acceptedOverride`/`acceptedOverrideMissing`);
  4. **lands before deciding** — `landWorkingTree()` commits (or `--no-ff` merges the `consolidationBranch`) *before* any state flip; if the loom produced build output but nothing landed, the accept **throws** and records an `accept-aborted` event instead of ever reaching `done` void.

### Loom ↔ Chat session linkage

A `Chat` (`chats.json`) optionally carries `loomId` + `role` (`"planner" | "steerer" | "escalation"`), set once a chat session becomes the vehicle for scoping, steering, or discussing a specific loom. This is the only cross-reference from the web-owned store back into core's `Loom` entity; core itself has no pointer back to a chat (a loom's own `attempts[].sessionId` records the Claude Agent SDK session id used for that attempt, which is a different id space than the chat UI's `Chat.id`, though the two commonly coincide since `Chat.id` is defined as "= SDK session id").

### Watches (reactor registration)

`Watch` records (`watches.json`) tie a `loomId` to a `sessionId` and a set of `triggerStates` (default `DEFAULT_TRIGGER_STATES`). `watches.ts` is a passive registry only — core has no reactor loop; the web app is expected to poll/react on trigger states (per the core scan's finding — no web-side reactor loop was independently located in this pass beyond the registry itself and the SSE-oriented `session-log.ts`/events routes).

## Migration & Compatibility Strategy

There is no versioned schema-migration framework (no migration functions keyed off a `version` number, no Prisma/Drizzle-style migration files). Compatibility is handled by four narrower, verified mechanisms:

1. **One-shot directory/filename migration.** `looms.ts:ensureMigrated()` runs once per process: if `~/.telar/runs/` exists but `~/.telar/looms/` does not, it `renameSync`s the directory and leaves a symlink (`runs` → `looms`) for back-compat; within each loom dir, a legacy `run.json` is renamed to `loom.json` if `loom.json` doesn't already exist. Guarded so it never throws (best-effort).

2. **Additive zod schemas with defaults.** Every schema in `schemas.ts` favors `.optional()` / `.default(...)` for new fields (e.g. `Loom.relaxedCoverage?`, `Charter.requirements?`, `ContractAssertion.subjective?`, `ProjectManifest.verifyCommand?`). A record written by an older version of the code parses cleanly under a newer schema — absent fields simply default. There is no schema-version bump or forward-migration step; "migration" here means "the new optional field is simply undefined on old records," verified by the extensive "additive / flag-off byte-identical" commentary throughout `schemas.ts`.

3. **Self-healing manifest cache.** `manifest.ts:getProject()` restores a wiped `telar.yaml` from the `projects.json` registry's cached copy (see [Storage Architecture](#storage-architecture)) — a resilience mechanism, not a schema migration (a present-but-outdated-shape `telar.yaml` still round-trips through the *current* `ProjectManifest` schema on every load; there is no field-renaming or version-detection logic).

4. **Home-relative path migration for accounts.** `accounts.ts:load()` rewrites any `AccountProfile.configDir` that is an absolute path under the *current* home into a portable `"~/..."` form on read (`toHomeRelative`), persisting the change only if something actually moved. This is a narrow, single-field, idempotent migration — not a general schema versioning mechanism.

**None found:** no `SCHEMA_VERSION` constant gating a migration function; no down-migrations; no data-migration CLI or script under `scripts/`; no database (hence no `ALTER TABLE`-equivalent). The `version` fields present in several store shapes (`SecretFile.version`, `AccountRegistry.version`, the OAuth store's `version`, `VerificationContract.version`, `ServersConfig.version`, `ThreadWorkflow.version`) are read back but, as verified in each store's read function, are not currently branched on to select a parse path — they default (`.default(1)` in the zod cases, `?? 1` in the plain-TS cases) and are otherwise inert, reserved for a future migration path that does not yet exist in code.
